facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin
A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin

concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E support this diagnosis.
The combination of liver masses, epithelioid tumor cells, and immunohistochemical staining for melanocytic markers suggests a primary liver melanoma.
The presence of multiple liver masses and melanocytic tumor cells raises the possibility of metastatic melanoma to the liver.
The finding of a liver mass could also be consistent with a hepatic adenoma, although the presence of melanocytic markers makes this less likely.
The liver mass could also represent focal nodular hyperplasia, although the absence of typical imaging features and the presence of melanocytic markers make this diagnosis less likely.
The elevated liver enzymes could be consistent with hepatitis, although the absence of other typical features and the presence of melanocytic markers make this diagnosis less likely.
The elevated liver enzymes could also be consistent with autoimmune hepatitis, although the absence of other typical features and the presence of melanocytic markers make this diagnosis less likely.

The elevated liver enzymes could also be consistent with primary biliary cholangitis, although the absence of other typical features and the presence of melanocytic markers make this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F09: Multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver suggest a malignant process, which could be primary or metastatic.
rationales.F10: Epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments are characteristic of melanocytic tumors.
rationales.F11: Diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E is highly suggestive of a melanocytic tumor, particularly melanoma.
